data.name: Barnabas
data.gender_notes: Barnabas is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek name 'Barnabas', meaning 'son of Encouragement'. In the New Testament, Barnabas was a disciple of Jesus and a key leader in the early Christian church. He was known for his generosity and encouragement of new believers. The name Barnabas carries the meaning “Son of Encouragement” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Barnabas usually hope their child will grow to embody son of encouragement and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes compassion, generosity, and encouragement in the Christian faith.
data.etymology: Barnabas belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Son of Encouragement.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Barnabas total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

in_hebrew.name: ברנבאס
in_hebrew.meaning: בן נבאס - בן נבואה או בן התנבא
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם ברנבאס מקורו במילה הארמית בר נבא, שפירושה בן הנבואה או בן התנבא. השם נגזר משתי מילים: בר, שפירושו בן, ו נבא, שפירושו נבואה. השם ברנבאס היה שמו של אחד מתלמידי ישוע הנוצרי, המוזכר בברית החדשה, ופעל כשליח וכמיסיונר.

in_greek.name: Βαρνάβας
in_greek.long_meaning: Ὁ Βαρνάβας προέρχεται ἀπὸ τὸ Ἀραμαϊκὸ ὄνομα Βαρ-נבא, τὸ ὁποῖο σημαίνει υἱὸς τῆς προφητείας ἢ υἱὸς τῆς παρακλήσεως. Στὴν Καινή Διαθήκη, ὁ Βαρνάβας ἦταν ἕνας τῶν μαθητῶν τοῦ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ σημαντικός ἀπόστολος καὶ ιεραπόστολος στὴν πρώιμη Εκκλησία.

in_latin.name: Barnabas
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Barnabas derivatur ex aramaico vocabulo Bar-naba, quod significat filium prophetiae. In Novo Testamento, Barnabas fuit unus ex discipulis Iesu Christi et apostolus importantissimus in Ecclesia primitiva.

in_english.name: Barnabas
in_english.meaning: Son of prophecy or son of encouragement
in_english.long_meaning: The name Barnabas originates from the Aramaic term 'Bar-naba,' meaning 'son of prophecy' or 'son of encouragement.' In the New Testament, Barnabas was a companion of Saint Paul and an early Christian missionary. The name symbolizes a person who brings encouragement and is associated with prophetic gifts.

data.cultural_impact: Barnabas is synonymous with encouragement and support, not just in the biblical context but also in our day-to-day lives. The name is a reminder of the importance of lifting each other up and creating a nurturing environment for personal growth and development. Barnabas is a popular name among various Christian communities and continues to inspire kindness, loyalty, and compassion.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Barnabas carries deep spiritual significance as it represents the virtues of encouragement, generosity, and unity in faith. It is a powerful reminder of the role spiritual leaders and mentors play in the spiritual journeys of others. In times of doubt, comfort, and growth, the name Barnabas serves as a source of inspiration and hope, nurturing the seed of faith and guiding us towards a deeper connection with the divine.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Barnabas, meaning "son of encouragement," embodies the spirit of consolation and support in the Christian community. He was a companion and mentor to Saul (later known as Paul), encouraging him to spread the gospel despite his past persecutions of Christians. Barnabas' role as a beacon of hope and acceptance is a testament to the transformative power of faith and compassion.

biblical_reference.note: Barnabas is mentioned as a companion of Paul in several New Testament passages.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Acts 4:36, 11:22-26, 13:1-3, 14:4, 4 Maccabees 4:6 The name Barnabas carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Barnabas was a Levite and companion of the Apostle Paul, known for his generosity and his role in the early Christian church.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Barnabas remains relevant in modern Christian society, representing a bridge between traditional Biblical values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Christian names.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted Christian named Peter Barnabas in London, United Kingdom credits much of their spiritual journey to their name Barnabas, which means "Son of Encouragement". They believe their name has been a blessing and reminder of God's presence in their life.
